provenance.accuracy: Standish Table 2a fit for the 3000 BC-AD 3000 window has JPL-stated nominal errors for Saturn of about 1000 arcsec in ecliptic longitude, 100 arcsec in ecliptic latitude, and 4000 (x1000 km) in heliocentric distance (approx_pos.html accuracy table). JPL's page also states that for Jupiter through Neptune the Table 2b correction terms 'must' be applied over this window; this app implements Table 2a ONLY, so Saturn's modeled position omits that correction. Quantifying the omission from Saturn's own Table 2b terms (b=0.00025899, c=-0.13434469, s=0.87320147, f=38.35125000, applied to the mean anomaly as b*T^2 + c*cos(f*T) + s*sin(f*T), T in Julian centuries from J2000): the periodic part alone has amplitude sqrt(c^2+s^2) = 0.88 deg regardless of epoch (so even near J2000, at T=0, the omitted constant term c contributes about -0.13 deg by itself); the quadratic part b*T^2 grows with distance from J2000 and reaches about 0.65 deg at the 3000 BC end of the range (T=-50 centuries) versus about 0.03 deg at the AD 3000 end (T=+10 centuries). So the omission can add on the order of 0.1-0.9 deg of extra mean-anomaly (and roughly similar heliocentric-longitude) error near the present era, growing to on the order of 1-1.5 deg near 3000 BC - on top of, not instead of, the ~0.28 deg (1000 arcsec) baseline Table-2a error above. Rotation is the secular linear IAU model only (pck00011.tpc BODY699 constant + rate terms); this kernel carries no periodic/nutation terms for Saturn, but the linear PM rate itself represents Saturn's IAU System III (radio/magnetic-field) rotation period, not the real, latitude-dependent differential rotation of the visible cloud deck. Rings are drawn as a single-scattering slab from a 2048-texel radial profile resampled from Solar System Scope's ring alpha map, calibrated on the Cassini Division's inner edge and the Encke Gap against the NSSDC ring fact sheet, with the A ring's outer edge as the check; ring particles and thickness are not modelled. absoluteMagnitude (-8.91) is NSSDC's ring-excluded V(1,0), so the single value here cannot capture how much brighter Saturn actually appears when its rings are present and open - real apparent brightness varies by roughly half a magnitude to a full magnitude or more across Saturn's ~29.5-year orbit as the ring-opening angle (and thus reflected ring light) changes. The albedo triple [0.53, 0.51, 0.43] is a stylistic per-channel split of the single published scalar geometric albedo (NSSDC's wavelength-independent 0.499, and the triple's mean is 0.49); it approximates Saturn's pale gold cast and is not a per-channel measurement. The shipped Mars record splits its own scalar flat for the same reason. The texture is a colour map, not a photometric measurement, and does not carry the albedo: the flat albedo above is what the Lambert model scales. The texture carries the globe only; the ring system is absent from it, which is why the record asks for rings as an enhancement rather than requiring one.
provenance.attribution: JPL Solar System Dynamics (orbit); NAIF / IAU Working Group (rotation); NASA NSSDC (physical parameters and ring geometry); Solar System Scope / INOVE (texture).
provenance.coverage: Heliocentric Saturn over 3000 BC to AD 3000, using Table 2a only (the mandatory Table 2b correction terms for this window are recorded in provenance.accuracy but not implemented). The saturn-2k texture ships with the app; the record falls back to a flat albedo if it is ever absent. The rings-profile asset ships with the app; builds without rings/1 draw Saturn without rings.
